overview: Driver apps maintain WebSockets to a location gateway. The gateway updates city-sharded Redis GEO sets and a separate per-driver heartbeat-expiry index, since GEO members do not have individual key TTLs. Matching queries fresh candidates and claims a driver with a fenced conditional state transition. Trips persist in SQL; payments use an external provider.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative active fleet: 1M drivers pinging every 5 seconds.
estimation.result: Location writes dominate trip creation and have short useful lifetimes.
estimation.implication: Shard geo state by region/city; persist trip assignments separately from ephemeral location data.

entityDetails.purpose: Authoritative trip state and driver assignment.
accessPatterns: Create a trip; conditionally claim one driver; advance the trip state.
constraints: A conditional write/fenced lease prevents two trips from claiming the same driver.
relationships: driver_id links the durable assignment to a fresh DriverLocation candidate; the geo lookup alone does not claim ownership.

entityDetails.purpose: Recent location and availability used for matching.
accessPatterns: Update location from pings; query nearby available drivers.
constraints: Reject stale timestamps and expire drivers from search after missed heartbeats; Redis GEO members require explicit per-member expiry logic.
relationships: Trip records the accepted assignment separately from ephemeral location membership.

apiDetails.purpose: Start a trip request and asynchronous matching.
apiDetails.rationale: A geo candidate is not an assignment; conditionally claim before notifying the driver.

apiDetails.purpose: Report driver location with a bounded update rate.
apiDetails.rationale: Kafka mode can use HTTP batch ingestion for the same message shape; ordering is per driver, not global.

apiDetails.purpose: Accept a current trip offer without racing an expired or reassigned lease.
apiDetails.rationale: Accept only the current unexpired driver offer; reject stale versions and repeated claims from another driver.

flows.title: Update location and match a rider

steps.title: Driver app → LB → Location gateway → Redis GEO (per city)
steps.explanation: Validate location sequence, update GEO membership and track per-driver heartbeat expiry.

steps.title: Rider app → LB → Matching Service → Redis GEO (per city)
steps.explanation: Search fresh available drivers and atomically claim one under a fenced offer.

steps.title: Matching Service → Trip Service → Trips DB
steps.explanation: Create the authoritative assigned trip; compensate a failed claim/commit boundary.

steps.title: Matching Service → Push
steps.explanation: Notify the selected driver with the offer version.

steps.title: Location gateway → Trip channels → Location gateway
steps.explanation: Relay trip events across socket gateways.

steps.title: Trip Service → Trips DB
steps.explanation: Accept only the current valid assignment; release expired offers conditionally.

failureCases.scenario: Two matchers select the same nearby driver
failureCases.handling: Only one conditional availability claim succeeds; retry the losing matcher with another candidate. Expire stale location membership and fence late acceptance of an expired offer.

alternatives: Use WebSockets and city Redis GEO for low-latency disposable location state. Use a replayable location stream and region indexers for rebuilds and analytics, while monitoring location lag. Both need exclusive driver claims.
